comparison: Both strongly support the CRISPR/Cas9 knockout validation (C20-C23, C68). OpenEval emphasizes multiple independent validation methods with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers explicitly praised the novel tool development (C58) and found validation compelling with no concerns raised.

Both support the electrophysiological findings (C24, C25) showing increased sIPSC frequency with presynaptic effects. OpenEval also addresses discrepancies with prior work (C69, C70), which peer reviewers acknowledge separately in R13. Both find the cellular mechanism plausible.

Both support reduced spontaneous activity findings (C26, C27, C28). OpenEval emphasizes preserved correlation structure and gain modulation interpretation (C77). Peer reviewers found the imaging approach rigorous and convincing without raising concerns about these findings.

Both support the dissociation between reduced response magnitude (C29, C30) and preserved orientation selectivity (C31). OpenEval emphasizes gain modulation interpretation (C78). Peer reviewers explicitly recognized this dissociation as a key finding with no concerns.

Both support impaired reliability findings (C32). OpenEval additionally discusses GLM modeling (C33, C34) and general reliability deficit interpretation (C79), which peer reviewers address separately in R6. Peer reviewers explicitly mentioned reliability as an important finding.

Partial overlap on GLM modeling (C33, C34, C79). OpenEval focuses on reliability and encoding impairment. Peer reviewers praised the advanced statistical modeling approach and found conclusions about coordinated activity and information encoding rigorous and convincing.

Strong agreement on population coordination findings (C35-C38, C74, C76). Both support the dissociation between preserved pairwise correlations and impaired population-level coordination. OpenEval emphasizes GLM capturing higher-order interactions; peer reviewers praised advanced statistical modeling.

Strong agreement on impaired population decoding (C39-C43, C80). Both support that reduced correlations reflect degraded coordination rather than beneficial decorrelation (C72, C73). OpenEval notes causality is inferred; peer reviewers found the study rigorous and convincing.

Perfect agreement on overarching conclusions (C2-C5, C45). Both strongly support that astrocytes actively regulate visual processing. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive multi-level evidence; peer reviewers recognized novel insights and important role of GAT3 in visual information processing.

Both address novelty of CRISPR tool. OpenEval supports novelty claim (C58) and speculates on applications (C59). Peer reviewers explicitly praised the tool as an important development in the field with potential broader applications.

Partial overlap on speculative applications (C59). OpenEval marks this as reasonable speculation given proof-of-concept. Peer reviewers implicitly support these speculations as reasonable extensions of convincing findings.

Both support pharmacological data (C66, C67). OpenEval notes high variability motivated genetic approach. Peer reviewers raised no concerns, providing implicit acceptance as supporting data consistent with genetic knockout results.

Both support Gat3 expression characterization (C18, C19). OpenEval describes this as confirmatory finding consistent with literature. Peer reviewers raised no concerns, providing implicit acceptance as important context for experimental manipulations.

Both rate mechanistic speculations (C48-C50) as uncertain. OpenEval notes these are explicitly speculative and not directly tested. Peer reviewers found overall mechanism plausible but did not explicitly validate specific hypotheses, leaving them uncertain.

Partial overlap on speculative claims (C56, C57). OpenEval marks as uncertain, acknowledging limitations and alternative explanations. Peer reviewers similarly found these speculative mechanistic interpretations uncertain despite overall positive reception.

Minimal overlap on background literature (C56). OpenEval notes this represents prior work rather than current findings. Peer reviewers did not question established background knowledge that provides scientific foundation.

Minimal overlap on correlation-decoding dissociation (C54). OpenEval supports this finding as well-documented. Peer reviewers recognized this as demonstrating functional consequences of reduced coordination.

Partial overlap on temporal organization interpretation (C55, C81). OpenEval supports these claims as reasonable though mechanisms remain to be elucidated. Peer reviewers found these interpretive claims to be logical inferences from convincing data.
Minimal overlap on discrepancies with prior work (C70). OpenEval marks as uncertain speculation about why results differ. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about this scholarly contextualization.
Minimal overlap on coordination mechanism (C75). OpenEval marks as uncertain/speculative. Peer reviewers also found this speculative despite overall positive reception of the work.

Partial overlap on interpretive claims (C75). OpenEval marks C70 and C75 as uncertain speculative explanations. Peer reviewers support most interpretive claims (C55, C71-C73, C77-C78, C81) as logical inferences from convincing data, finding cellular mechanism plausible.

Minimal overlap on gain modulation interpretation (C77). OpenEval supports this interpretation as well-supported by dissociation between firing rate and correlations. Peer reviewers found this interpretive claim to be a logical inference from convincing data.

Minimal overlap on gain modulation interpretation (C78). OpenEval supports this as logically following from observed dissociation. Peer reviewers found this interpretive claim to be a logical inference from convincing data.

Partial overlap on discrepancies with prior literature (C69, C70). OpenEval marks C70 as uncertain speculation but appropriately acknowledges discrepancies. Peer reviewers did not raise concerns about this scholarly contextualization.

Peer reviewers supported extensive background/contextual claims (C1, C6-C15, C44, C46-C47, C51-C52, C56, C60-C62, C65) from published literature. OpenEval did not create a separate result for these background claims, though some appear in other OpenEval results.
Peer reviewers supported speculative/interpretive claims (C59, C63, C64) as reasonable extensions of convincing findings. OpenEval addressed C59 in R9 but did not separately evaluate C63 and C64.
